text:
Both responses are correct on the main points. The word comes from *gangurru* in Guugu Yimithirr, it was recorded in 1770 near Cooktown, the "I don't understand" claim is a myth, and Haviland's 1970s work confirmed the word's meaning. Both stay under 120 words (A is about 103, B about 109).

The difference is in the reasoning about the myth. A mostly retells the myth's content (the crew pointing and misunderstanding the reply). B adds a plausible account of how the myth arose: later Europeans found that Aboriginal people elsewhere didn't recognize the word, because Australia has many distinct languages. B also names Banks alongside Cook and says why the story persists. These additions are accurate and useful.

B is slightly better.

Verdict: B
